title: $\cO_E$ is the profinite limit of its finite quotients $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, with its extending absolute value $|\cdot|_E$, ring of integers $\cO_E=\{x\in E:|x|_E\le1\}$, uniformizer $\pi_E$, finite quotient rings $A_n=\cO_E/\pi_E^n\cO_E$ $(n\ge1)$ and transition homomorphisms $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $q_n\colon\cO_E\to A_n$ be the reduction maps. Give $\cO_E$ the topology of $|\cdot|_E$, each $A_n$ the discrete topology, and $\varprojlim_nA_n=\{(b_n)\in\prod_{n\ge1}A_n: b_{n+1}\mapsto b_n\text{ for all }n\}$ the subspace topology of the product topology, with coordinatewise ring operations. Then:

1. The map $q=(q_n)_n\colon\cO_E\to\varprojlim_nA_n$ is an isomorphism of rings and a homeomorphism.
2. $\cO_E$ is a profinite space: compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected.
3. For every finite set $Q$ with the discrete topology and every continuous surjection $g\colon\cO_E\to Q$ there is an $n\ge1$ such that $g$ factors as $g=h\circ q_n$ for a map $h\colon A_n\to Q$; such an $h$ is unique, and $g$ then factors uniquely through $q_m$ for every $m\ge n$.

proof.text: Apply the uniformizer-coset neighbourhood basis theorem. The integer ring is the closed unit ball in the proper spectral-norm field, hence compact and Hausdorff. Its positive reduction maps are locally constant by the coset basis.

Construct the ring homomorphism taking each integer to its compatible sequence of reductions. Equality of all reductions implies equality because each neighbourhood contains a coset. For a compatible family, its coordinate fibres are nonempty closed nested subsets of the compact integer ring; their intersection is nonempty. This proves bijectivity. The map is continuous coordinatewise, hence is a homeomorphism from a compact space to a Hausdorff space. Each reduction is locally constant, so is constant on every preconnected subset. Joint injectivity then makes every preconnected subset a subsingleton, proving total disconnectedness.

A continuous map to a discrete set is locally constant. Choose at every point a positive reduction fibre on which the map is constant. A finite subcover exists by compactness. The maximum of the exponents makes the map constant on every fibre at that exponent and at all higher levels. Define each factor on quotient representatives; fibrewise constancy proves well-definedness and quotient surjectivity proves uniqueness.
